#en: They say this place was built for mundane things like spectral analysis and rock samples. Funny, because nobody I have met can tell the same story twice about what really went on in these labs. When the resupply shuttle dropped me here last week, the pilot called it a "paper graveyard." The maintenance tech who greeted me just said "keep your head down and never, ever ask about missing ships" then laughed like it was a joke he wished it was.  \n\nI started hearing the rest in pieces. One version says some freelance navigator sold private shortcuts to smugglers, then used this module to scrub the evidence when convoys started vanishing. Another has him on a corporate retainer, tuning routes so insurance never had to pay out. A third paints him as some righteous saboteur trying to expose a system built on acceptable losses. Same name, different motives, always a trail of dead lanes behind him. Every retelling shifts a detail, like people are trying to talk around something they still do not want to see straight. All I know for certain is that the more I dig through these half-archived logs, the more I find the same hands adjusting jump patterns without ever signing them, and the more the room feels crowded even when I am alone.
zh: 他们说这地方是为光谱分析和岩石采样这类平凡事建的。好笑的是，我见过的人里没有一个能把这些实验室里究竟发生过什么讲成同一个版本。上周补给穿梭机把我送到这里时，飞行员管它叫"纸坟场"。迎接我的维护技工只说了一句"低着头干活，永远、永远别问失踪飞船的事"，然后笑起来，像那是个他但愿只是玩笑的玩笑。\n\n余下的我是零零碎碎听来的。一种说法是某个自由领航员把私人捷径卖给走私贩，然后在运输队开始失踪时用这个模块擦掉证据。另一种说法是他受企业聘用，调校航线好让保险公司永远不必赔付。第三种把他描绘成某种正义的破坏者，试图揭穿一个建立在"可接受损失"之上的系统。同一个名字，不同的动机，身后总留下一串死掉的航道。每一次转述都会挪动一个细节，像人们试图绕着某个他们仍不愿看清的东西说话。我唯一确定的是：我越是翻检这些半归档的日志，就越发现同一双手在调整跃迁图案却从不署名；而房间也越来越显得拥挤，哪怕只有我一个人。

#en: I was supposed to be cataloguing soil samples this week. That is what the assignment packet said when they shipped me out here to this forgotten station, just another junior tech shuffling data no one on Jemison will ever read twice. Funny thing, though, about being the one who actually clears the archives; you see what people thought they had erased.  \n\nThere is a whole chain of access logs with gaps where there should not be any. Requests that hop from our lab to freight registries, then vanish mid-route, like somebody yanked the cord on the connection and hoped no one would notice the scorch mark. And buried under a stack of mislabeled experiment files I found a reference to a private relay, tagged only by coordinates and a contractor ID that got my supervisor suddenly very quiet. She told me to delete it, then later asked if I had "seen anything unusual" in that directory, like she was afraid of the answer. Out in the common room, the older staff still swap stories about lost convoys and a man who could twist corridors with a stylus stroke, always looking over their shoulders when they do. Someone wanted this trail dead, but they missed a step, and now I know exactly which off-grid node their phantom connection pointed to.
zh: 这周我本该给土壤样本编目。他们把我发配到这座被遗忘的空间站时，任务包里是这么写的——又一个整理数据的初级技工，整理那些杰米森上永远不会有人读第二遍的数据。不过，真正动手清档案的人有个好处：你能看见别人以为已经擦掉的东西。\n\n有一整条访问日志链，在本来不该有空缺的地方留着空缺。一些请求从我们实验室跳到货运登记处，然后在半路消失，像有人把连接的线一把扯断，还指望没人会注意到焦痕。而在一堆贴错标签的实验文件底下，我发现了一处私人中继站的引用，只标着坐标和一个承包商 ID——看到它，我主管忽然变得非常安静。她叫我把它删掉，后来又问我有没有在那目录里"看到什么不寻常的东西"，像她害怕听到答案。在外面公共室里，那些年长的员工还在交换关于失踪运输队、以及一个能用一笔星标划动就把走廊掰弯的人的故事，讲的时候总是回头张望。有人想让这条痕迹死掉，可他们漏了一步；如今我确切知道，他们那条幽灵连接指向的是哪个不上网的节点。

#en:
I keep replaying the moment the relay flagged that first spike.

It was late, nothing moving but survey drones and commuter buses, when the grid squealed about a ship cutting through restricted sky like it owned the air. I pulled the scan, saw the vector, and knew it was wrong in the way that makes your teeth hurt. Sent it up the line. Got a one-line reply: "Instrument drift. Clear and proceed." Simple. Neat. Done.

But if it was drift, why did the same ghost signature slide past again three nights later, and again after that, always just outside where the charts say people are allowed to be

I dug through archived diagnostics and found the old relay listed as "retired," except it is not. You can hear it in the floorplates, feel it when the consoles buzz a little hotter during those passes. Everyone talks about it in half-sentences and lowered voices, like saying too much might make the pattern solid enough to blame on someone real.

The truth feels small, one obvious step no one wants to write down, and somehow that makes it harder to grab. So I copy the scans onto a spare slate, lock it in my locker, and tell myself I am imagining things while the same nameless ship keeps sliding through the same forbidden slice of sky.
zh:
我一直在重放中继站第一次标出那道尖峰的那一刻。

那是深夜，除了勘测无人机和通勤班车外别无动静，电网却尖叫起来，说有一艘飞船切开受限天空，像那片空域是它家的。我调出扫描，看见那个矢量，就知道它错得让人牙酸。我把它上报。得到一行回复："仪器漂移。放行，继续。"简单。干净。完事。

可如果那是漂移，为什么三个晚上后同样的幽灵特征又滑过了一次，之后又一次，永远在星图说人们被允许待的地方之外？

我翻遍存档诊断，发现那座旧中继站被列为"已退役"——可它没有。你能从甲板板里听见它，能在那些通过期间控制台嗡鸣稍微变热时感觉到它。人人都用半截句子和压低的声音谈论它，像说多了就会让那图案变得足够实体，好归咎到某个真实的人头上。

真相感觉很小，就是一个显而易见、没人愿意写下来的步骤；而不知怎的，这反而让它更难抓住。于是我把扫描拷到一块备用数据板上，锁进我的储物柜，并告诉自己是我在胡思乱想——与此同时，那艘始终无名的飞船仍不断滑过同一小片被禁的天空。

#en:
I am writing this with my back against a GalBank bulkhead, listening to the ship groan like it wants to fall out of orbit and be done with secrets.

Three years ago, give or take, I was running cargo through that nowhere depot the haulers use when they do not want questions. We were half-asleep, nursing cheap coffee, when the air on the dock went strange. Not a siren, not a fault, just this low tremor in the deckplates that set everyone's teeth on edge.

Some swear they saw a woman in coveralls at the access panel, hands buried in a conduit that should have been dead. Others say it was just a shadow and an overworked tech with a guilty conscience. All I know is the drives on three different ships tripped themselves offline inside an hour, and every log blamed "operator error."

Since then I keep hearing the same symbol described in different ports, the same name muttered like a curse, and the same story about systems that fail exactly the way an old buried report once predicted. Maybe it is all exaggeration. But when a GalBank vault ship like this one goes quiet in the same corridor, after the depot and that anonymous outpost, it starts to feel less like random bad luck and more like somebody is walking the map with a purpose.
zh:
我背靠着一面银河银行的舱壁写下这些，听着这艘船呻吟，像它想掉出轨道、把秘密一了百了。

大约三年前，我正把货物运过那座运货船员不想被问问题时会用的荒野补给站。我们半睡半醒地啜着廉价咖啡，码头的空气忽然变得不对劲。不是警报，不是故障，只是甲板板里一阵低沉的震颤，让所有人都牙根发紧。

有人赌咒说，他们在检修口看见一个穿工装的女人，双手埋在一条本该已死的导管里。另一些人说那不过是影子，和一个心里有鬼、累坏了的技工。我只知道，三艘不同的飞船在一小时内各自的驱动都自行离线了，而每一份日志都归咎于"操作员失误"。

从那以后，我不断在不同的港口听到同样的符号被描述，同样的名字被像咒骂一样嘟囔，同样的故事——关于一些系统的失效方式，恰好和一份埋藏已久的旧报告所预言的一样。也许那全是夸大。可当一艘像这样的银河银行金库船在同一条走廊里陷入沉寂时，在那座补给站和那座无名前哨站之后，它就开始显得不像随机的厄运，而更像有人带着某种目的在走过这张地图。

#en:
I remember when the first set of manifests crossed my desk. Same old stamps, same old shippers, nothing that would have raised so much as an eyebrow if I had been three cups of TerraBrew deep and half asleep. That is the problem. After a few years with the Trade Authority, the formats blur together, and "routine" becomes a kind of blindness. You stop asking why a freighter needs an extra hop, or why a fuel charge does not line up with the tonnage.

It is only now, sitting in a quiet office with the comms dimmed, that I see how much we let slide because it looked familiar. The routes that double back near the same empty regions. The insurance claims on ships that "misjumped" along those paths. The way certain names in the ledgers come and go like they are testing the waters, then vanish altogether. None of it screamed fraud or sabotage. It just hummed along under the noise of a thousand legitimate runs, invisible because it copied the shape of normal traffic so well.

I used to pride myself on knowing every quirk of Authority paperwork, every lazy habit captains had. Now I am wondering how long someone has been hiding inside that certainty, using our comfort with the usual patterns as cover to carve their own paths through the dark.
zh:
我记得第一批清单落到我桌上的样子。同样的老戳记，同样的老发货方，要是我喝了三杯地球酿酒、半睡半醒，这种单子连一根眉毛都抬不起来。问题就在这里。在贸易管理局待了几年之后，各种格式糊成一片，而"例行"变成了一种盲。你不再问为什么一艘货船要多跳一站，也不再问为什么一笔燃料费跟吨位对不上。

直到现在，坐在一间通讯调暗的安静办公室里，我才看清我们因为"看着眼熟"而放过了多少东西。那些绕回同一片空区域附近的航线。那些沿着这些路径"错误跃迁"的飞船的保险索赔。账簿上某些名字来来去去，像在试探水温，然后彻底消失。这一切都没喊出欺诈或破坏。它只是在上千趟合法航次的噪声底下嗡嗡运行，因为把正常交通的形状模仿得太好而变得隐形。

我以前自傲于熟悉管理局文书的每一个怪癖、船长们的每一个偷懒习惯。如今我在想，有人藏在这份确定感里已经多久了——利用我们对惯常图案的安心作掩护，在黑暗中凿出自己的路。

#en: I have been posted on this rock for eight months now, long enough that the hum of the equipment feels louder than my own thoughts. When I first arrived, the job was simple: compare traffic reports to corporate manifests, watch for the usual data skimming along the edges. Then someone upstairs pushed a firmware update through our routing tools and did not bother to brief anyone. The interface barely changed, just a few new flags, a different way it rounded jump estimates. Easy to ignore.\n\nExcept the patterns shifted. Routes that should have been clean started clipping the same thin corridor near that debris field; minor adjustments kept nudging freighters toward the same sparse beacons and forgotten relays. Our internal logs, the ones that used to double-check the math, began overwriting themselves in neat little windows of missing time. At first I chalked it up to bad code and lazy contractors. Now I am sitting on packet captures and mirrored archives that say otherwise, and I have a set of coordinates circled where three "unrelated" misjumps all pivoted off the same change order signed by the same analyst. Routines changed quietly, and nobody cared until the wreck counts lined up on my screen like someone had drawn a curve through them.
zh: 我在这块岩石上已经驻守八个月了，久到设备的嗡鸣声听起来比我自己的思绪还响。我刚来时，工作很简单：把交通报告和企业清单做对比，盯着那些照例在边缘揩油的数据。后来楼上有人通过我们的航路工具推了一次固件更新，却没费心通知任何人。界面几乎没变，只是多了几个标记，跃迁估算的取整方式变了一下。很容易忽略。\n\n可图案变了。那些本该干净的航线开始擦过碎片场附近同一条狭窄走廊；些微的调整不断把货船推向同一批稀疏的信标和被遗忘的中继站。我们那些原本用来复核算式的内部日志，开始在一段段整齐的缺失时间里自我覆盖。起初我把这归咎于糟糕的代码和懒惰的承包商。如今我手里握着数据包捕获和镜像存档，证明并非如此；我还圈出了一组坐标——三起"互不相关"的错误跃迁都是从同一名分析师签署的同一份变更单上拐走的。常规被悄悄改动了，而在残骸计数在我屏幕上排成一线、像有人画了条曲线穿过它们之前，没人在意。

#en:
I am recording this in case I do not make it back to delete the evidence.

The bunker still listens, even with half its panels gutted. Old UC protocols pinging empty sky, catching ghosts no one filed. I pulled the sweep from the night that cutter vanished. Buried in the noise were microbursts in restricted airspace, too clean to be random, stitched like beads on a line. Same signature shift every time, same altitude, same timing just outside the official corridor.

Cross-referenced it against patrol routes and derelict notices. Only one hull fits the gap: a light tactical frame listed as "maintenance extended" for the last eighteen months. Same ship that forwarded those weird redacted jump reports to this bunker and never logged a receipt.

Someone upstairs meant to come out here, match the scans to that hull, and shut whatever this is down. They queued the follow-up, then never showed. Maybe they got scared. Maybe they got paid.

I tracked the transponder echo. That tactical is drifting just off the grid, still answering to UC credentials like nothing is wrong. If there is a trail left to this pathfinder everyone keeps pretending not to know, it is sitting in that hull's logs, waiting for someone else to make the mistake of looking.
zh:
我录下这个，以防我没能回来删掉证据。

碉堡还在听着，哪怕一半面板被掏空了。旧联殖协议朝空荡的天空发着探测，捕捉着没人归档的鬼。我调出那艘切割船失踪当晚的扫描。埋在噪声里的，是受限空域中的微爆，干净得不像随机，像一串珠子缝在一条线上。每次都是同样的特征偏移，同样的高度，同样的时机，刚好在官方走廊之外。

我把它与巡逻路线和弃船通告交叉比对。只有一具船体对得上这道缺口：一个轻型战术框架，过去十八个月一直被列为"延长维护"。正是那艘把那些奇怪的涂黑跃迁报告转发给这座碉堡、却从未记录过签收的飞船。

楼上有人本打算来这儿，把扫描和那具船体对上，然后把这不知什么东西关掉。他们排好了后续，然后从没出现。也许他们害怕了。也许他们被收买了。

我追踪了应答器回波。那艘战术舰正漂在网格之外，仍在回应联殖凭证，像什么都没发生。如果说还有一条痕迹留在这个人人都假装不认识的探路者身上，它就躺在那具船体的日志里，等着别人犯下"去看一眼"的错误。

#en: East Division is the informal designation for a mixed support and escort cadre that operates in the shipping corridors surrounding the CB-6735 Trustsphere route network. Originally assembled from career hauler crews and a handful of former security pilots, the group built a reputation for steady, regulation-compliant work, the sort of people traders once described as "the boring ones you survive with." Recent months have marked a quiet change in both posture and temperament; reports note longer weapons drills, more sealed briefings, and deployments that linger near derelict tonnage and unlogged grav-scars. Off-duty, crew behavior has shifted from casual camaraderie to brittle, watchful silence: personnel who once swapped stories about shore leave now stand in long, shuffling lines at mess or resupply wondering when, exactly, they stopped feeling like transport hands and started feeling like expendable pieces in someone else's calculation. Rumors of sudden promotions, inexplicable demotions, and a few key figures who can bypass standard rotation boards suggest that internal politics, rather than flight hours, now decide who gets the safer patrol arcs and who is sent to shadow the ghosts that keep appearing near the Trustsphere's last known vectors.
zh: 东部分队是一支混合支援与护航队伍的非正式叫法，活动在 CB-6735 信托球号航线网络周边的航运走廊里。这支队伍最初由职业运货船员和少数前安保飞行员组成，以稳健、守规的作风赢得名声——商人曾形容他们是"那种能陪你活下来的无聊家伙"。近几个月来，他们的姿态与气质都发生了悄然变化；报告提到更长时间的武器操演、更多密封的简报，以及一些在弃船残骸和未入账重力伤痕附近徘徊的部署。下班后，船员的行为已从随意的同袍情谊转为紧绷、警觉的沉默：曾经交换休班故事的人，如今在食堂或补给处排着长长、挪动不安的队伍，琢磨着自己究竟是从何时起不再觉得自己是运输人员，而开始觉得是别人算盘里可牺牲的棋子。关于突然升职、莫名降职，以及少数能绕过标准轮换名单的关键人物的传言，都表明如今决定谁去跑更安全的巡逻弧线、谁被派去跟踪那些不断在信托球号最后已知矢量附近出现的幽灵的，是内部政治，而不是飞行时数。
